runtime.command_template: python tools/run_pinmame_harness.py --library <libpinmame> --game tz_92 --rom-path <vpinmame-roms> --work-dir <new-isolated-state> --handle-mechanics 1 --watch-switch 5 --watch-switch 7 --watch-switch 8 --watch-switch 22 --scenario tools/harness-scenarios/wpc-fliptronic/tz-clock-test-mech.json --dmd-dir <external-dmd-dir> --output <external-run.json>. The scenario holds public 22 released (coin door open) from power-up, leaves the fresh-NVRAM message loop with service Escape, walks the service menu with Enter and Up to T.16 CLOCK TEST (the 9.2 ROM inserts T.14 LAMP ROW/COLUMN and T.15 DIP SW. TEST before it), and starts and stops each operation with Enter, selecting the next with Up. The operation names are read from the DMD's top line in the retained frames. Outputs are polled about every 16 ms, so the per-operation seconds carry that resolution. Each operation window runs from the snapshot before its start press to the snapshot after its stop press (about 0.47 s longer than press to press); each CLOCK STOPPED window covers the four 0.25 s samples after the open or stop press. --handle-mechanics 1 turns on pinned PinMAME's own clock model (tz.c mech_add(0,&mechClock)), the setting the retained table uses, so the modelled clock moves and drives the eight clock optos, and the ROM's display shows its reading of them: the time, the minute-opto boxes 00/15/30/45 and the HOUR OPTOS boxes, named here by the labels page 1-18 prints under them (Hour 4 at the left to Hour 1 at the right). With the model on the power-up test report is empty, so this scenario drops the model-off walk's sound-revision and PRESS ENTER FOR MAIN MENU steps. A first attempt with the model-off scenario (retained as review-artifacts/twilight-zone-1993/clock-test-run3-mech-exploratory-wrong-menu-item) ended in T.3 SINGLE SWITCH for that reason and is not cited. The frames show a model driven by the ROM's outputs, not a physical clock.

source.attribution: Generated locally from pinned PinMAME and the user-authorized ROM corpus; ROM bytes remain external
source.manifest_algorithm: source.sha256 is the SHA-256 of the run folder's manifest.json exact bytes, written and checked by tools/build_external_evidence_manifest.py: compact canonical JSON with sorted keys, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False, plus one LF, listing every file under source.path except manifest.json and manifest.sha256 as {path, sha256, size} with POSIX relative paths sorted by path; manifest.sha256 beside it holds the same digest.
